chunks: It is He who made the earth subservient to you that you may travel all around it, and eat of things He has provided; and to Him will be your resurrection.
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about the purpose of the earth and human movement upon it?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse from Surah Al-Mulk (67:15) is often interpreted as a call to active engagement with the world, where 'traversing its slopes' signifies utilizing the earth's diverse resources for sustenance and spiritual growth. It underscores the concept of *tawhid* in creation, linking the physical act of consumption and movement directly to the metaphysical reality of resurrection (*al-nushur*), reminding believers that worldly provisions are temporary trusts from God.
